description:
crate-jmap-sharing-server/src/notification.rs:78-100 enforces RFC 9670 §3.3 ('only destroy is supported') at the HANDLER layer: every entry in create_map and update_map gets a SetError::Forbidden response without touching the backend. The doc comment at notification.rs:46-51 explicitly cites RFC 9670 §3.3.

Why this should be defended: a contributor reviewing the PLAN.md §2 'ShareNotification/set rejects creates and updates in the handler layer' might suggest pushing this enforcement into the backend trait for symmetry with Principal/set ('all permission decisions live in the backend'). That suggestion is wrong here. The RFC 9670 §3.3 rule is a PROTOCOL constraint on the ShareNotification object type, not a permission/policy decision. Every backend that handles ShareNotification has the SAME constraint. Putting it in every backend impl means 6 places to forget it; putting it in the handler is the spec contract being honored once.

This is also consistent with how VacationResponse is handled in jmap-mail-server (per PLAN.md §2 cross-reference).

Test coverage that locks this in: notification.rs:209-272 (set_create_returns_forbidden_not_created, set_update_returns_forbidden_not_updated). Removing the handler-layer check would break those tests immediately.
notes: Existing design defended — no code change needed. The handler-layer 'forbidden' enforcement for ShareNotification create/update is documented at notification.rs:46-51 with explicit RFC 9670 §3.3 citation, and locked in by tests set_create_returns_forbidden_not_created and set_update_returns_forbidden_not_updated. The defense bead exists to flag a future contributor's potential 'push it to the backend for symmetry' suggestion; the current shape is correct because RFC 9670 §3.3 is a protocol constraint on the object type, not a per-backend policy. (The .30 destroy-array refactor in this same epic preserves the handler-layer shape.)
title: Handler-layer 'forbidden' enforcement in ShareNotification/set with explicit RFC 9670 §3.3 citation
